translations.open-source-page.hero.lede: The whole platform is published under Apache 2.0 with the Commons Clause. Read it, fork it, run it on your own machine, build for your clients with it. None of that needs our permission.
translations.open-source-page.license.title: Apache 2.0, in plain words
translations.open-source-page.license.body: Four rights the licence grants you, and the one obligation it puts on you. The full text ships with the repository.
translations.open-source-page.data.title: Where your work actually sits
translations.open-source-page.data.lede: Three places, and you pick. The platform does not change behaviour depending on which one you choose.
translations.open-source-page.law.title: No lock-in to argue about
translations.open-source-page.law.lede: Every deliverable leaves as a file you own: the brand book as a PDF, the logo and its variants as a ZIP, the generated site and app as source code. What the platform keeps, and for how long, is written down — not described in a sales page.
translations.open-source-page.community.title: Decisions happen in the open
translations.open-source-page.community.body: The roadmap, the issues and the arguments are public. If a choice affects how your business runs, you get to be in the conversation.
translations.open-source-page.cta.title: Clone it, or just use it
translations.open-source-page.cta.body: Running IDEM yourself costs you a server. Running it here costs nothing until you keep something.
translations.open-source-page.clause.read.title: Read and audit all of it
translations.open-source-page.clause.read.description: Every line of the platform is public, including how your data is stored and which model handles which request.
translations.open-source-page.clause.host.title: Install it on your own servers
translations.open-source-page.clause.host.description: Run the whole platform inside your company, for your company. No licence fee, no call home.
translations.open-source-page.clause.clients.title: Deliver client work with it
translations.open-source-page.clause.clients.descript: Agencies and freelancers can use IDEM to build for their clients, and charge for that work as they always have.
translations.open-source-page.clause.modify.title: Change it and share the change
translations.open-source-page.clause.modify.descripti: Fork it, patch it, redistribute it, as long as the copyright notices stay in place.
translations.open-source-page.clause.sell.title: Resell IDEM itself
translations.open-source-page.clause.sell.description: The Commons Clause added to the licence rules out selling the software, or hosting it as a paid service of your own. Write to us if that is what you need.
translations.open-source-page.hosting.managed.title: Our managed hosting
translations.open-source-page.hosting.managed.descrip: The default. You create a project, we keep the machines running, and your deliverables are downloadable at any point.
translations.open-source-page.hosting.vps.title: Your own VPS
translations.open-source-page.hosting.vps.description: Point iDeploy at a server you rent and it builds there instead. The provider, the country and the invoice are yours.
translations.open-source-page.hosting.onPremise.title: A machine in your office
translations.open-source-page.hosting.onPremise.descr: The full platform installs from the repository with Docker. Nothing leaves the building, including the prompts.
translations.open-source-page.place.github.descriptio: The code, the issues and the roadmap. Pull requests are read.
translations.open-source-page.place.issues.name: Report a bug
translations.open-source-page.place.issues.descriptio: Open an issue on the repository. Bugs reported in the open get fixed in the open.
translations.open-source-page.place.releases.name: Release notes
translations.open-source-page.place.releases.descript: What changed, version by version, with the commits behind each line.
